findings.title: `orbit-explore-modifications`' own five-section requirement is left unmodified and contradicts the new six-section format
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: ENUMERATE] Baseline orbit/specs/orbit-explore-modifications/spec.md:117-124 (`Requirement: explore.md five-section convention`) states five sections in fixed order and its `Initial stub structure` scenario asserts all five are present. The change modifies only orbit-conventions' copy. After sync, baseline holds TWO contradictory format definitions and the explore body's own governing requirement still forbids the section this change exists to add. Add a MODIFIED block carrying the FULL baseline text with Mechanism inserted and the stub scenario updated (same capability — no ceiling cost), plus a base_fingerprints entry.

findings.title: The re-entry requirement contradicts the unmodified `Three invocation modes supported` Mode B scenario
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: COHERE] Baseline orbit/specs/orbit-explore-modifications/spec.md:31-32: WHEN `/orbit:explore <name>` is invoked and `orbit/explore/<name>/` does not exist THEN the command CREATES the staging directory. That WHEN is exactly true in the promoted-name case, where the new requirement says create NOTHING. Two baseline requirements would prescribe opposite acts for one condition — the COHERE class this change names as most-recurring. Carry `Three invocation modes supported` as MODIFIED: guard Mode B's WHEN with `and no active change of that name exists`, and update its stub-section list.

findings.title: The six-move set is not closed: the derivation generates no move for the mechanism's OUTPUT or for its cost/termination, and a defect on this program's own record lands outside it
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: ENUMERATE] The derivation sentence is `an assembly of parts computing outputs from inputs under constraints`, but the table assigns moves to facts, input domain, parts, computation, purpose and context — OUTPUTS and constraints-as-resources get none. EXECUTE is `wrong output on a member it does handle`, which does not cover a mechanism producing NO output in feasible time. This change's own explore.md Case 1 records exactly that defect — `assignCadence` exponential blowup, classed `(c) never confronted` — and R-crc-7 names a further class, testing EXISTENCE where the property needed was USABILITY. A third candidate: a rule that is correct and never fires. Per D-rc13-13 a classification falsifies but never closes, and Case 7 classified only rc03a's fifteen; rc02's four were never run against the set. Either derive the missing moves (OUTPUT/usability; FEASIBILITY) or re-declare the set as BOUNDED with an explicit residual — do not ship it as DERIVED-and-closed.

findings.title: The maturity-rung change is not implementable from the spec: no rule-closure input exists, and nothing names one
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: EXECUTE] `maturityRecommendation(name, decisionsCaptured, openQuestionsCount)` (explore-counter.ts:146-163) is fed only by `countExploreFile`, which counts top-level items under `## Decisions` / `## Open questions` (explore-counter.ts:101-123) and knows nothing of rules, domains or a Mechanism section; emit-composition.ts:906-918 passes those two counts and nothing else. Task 4.1 says the function `gains the rule-closure input` and 4.4 says the emit `carries whatever field 4.1 reads` — the field is never named, typed or assigned an owner. Two consequences: the rung's spec requires NAMING the open rules so a boolean will not do; and if the field is caller-supplied it is self-classification, the exact dodge D-rc13-14 was written to remove, while if it is engine-derived the spec must say how a grammar-independent test becomes machine-decidable, which design.md declares a non-goal. Name the field, its shape, who computes it, and whether it is engine-owned or a payload field.

findings.title: `every RULE in Decisions` has an unclosed domain: superseded, out-of-scope and handed-away rules make the Mature rung unreachable
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: ENUMERATE] The Decisions section is append-only and keeps superseded entries annotated in place — this change's own D-rc13-8 and D-rc13-9 are rules with domains that were never closed, and D-rc13-3/D-rc13-4 are rules the file itself records as `NO — domain not closed` and hands to rc08/rc03. Under the requirement as written, any exploration that ever supersedes or defers a rule can never render Mature again. State the disposition of every member of `rules in Decisions`: superseded entries, entries assigned to another stage, and explorations with no Mechanism section at all. A blanket default here is precisely what R-crc-7 forbids.

findings.title: No stated disposition for a legacy explore.md with no Mechanism section — and the Migration Plan asserts a behavior the engine has no way to produce
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: ENUMERATE] `Migration Plan: None. An exploration with no rules is unaffected … absence renders as no rules recorded rather than as a violation.` Nothing renders anything about rules today, and the engine cannot distinguish `no rules` from `rules whose closure was never declared`. Treat-as-closed makes the requirement vacuous for every pre-existing exploration and gameable by deleting the section; treat-as-open changes the recommendation for existing staging dirs, contradicting `Migration: None`. State the absent-section rule in the SPEC, not the design.

findings.title: `Four mutually-exclusive maturity states cover the full grid` is false once the closure dimension is added
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: ENUMERATE] The grid gains a third axis, so the cells are five: Early, Mid, Mature, Stalled, and the new 4+/<=1/OPEN-domain cell, described in prose at line 12 but absent from the bulleted grid. Add it as a named fifth state or restate the sentence. Also state precedence for 4+ decisions AND >1 open questions AND open domains — as written Stalled wins and the open-domain gap is never named, so exit criterion 2 is silently unmet in that cell.

findings.title: The withheld-Mature rendering still surfaces `/orbit:propose`, contradicting the Stalled precedent in the same requirement
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: COHERE] Mid's text is `continue thinking, or /orbit:propose <name> if ready to formalize`, so `renders the MID rung's deferring language` means an exploration with an OPEN RULE DOMAIN is still offered propose — while Stalled deliberately withholds it because high open-question count signals NOT-ready regardless of decision count. An unclosed rule domain is at least as strong a not-ready signal. Either justify the asymmetry in the requirement text or render the gap case without the propose alternative, and then fix the line saying the alternative is present for Mid and Mature only.

findings.title: 23 tasks is over R-crc-1's `under 20 tasks` ceiling, while the change declares itself AT the ceiling on capabilities only
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: CONFORM] R-crc-1 is four-dimensional: <=3 capabilities, ~12 requirements, ~40 KB delta, under 20 tasks. The change is 3 capabilities / 4 requirements / small delta but 23 tasks, and proposal.md and design.md both assert AT-ceiling on capabilities without mentioning the task count. Either state the overage and why it does not trigger R-crc-9, or fold tasks. Note the missing deltas flagged above will ADD tasks.

findings.title: Propose's consume-mode mapping has no destination for the Mechanism section — the stage's deliverable is dropped at promotion
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: ENUMERATE] orbit/specs/orbit-propose-modifications/spec.md:29 (`Section-to-artifact mapping`) and the body table at propose.ts:174-182 enumerate Premise / Decisions / Open questions / Considered & out / References. With no Mechanism row, the closed enumerations — the artifact this stage exists to produce — reach the change directory and inform nothing. `orbit-propose-modifications` is a FOURTH capability, so per R-crc-9 the sanctioned moves are to SPLIT (a follow-on stage owning propose's consumption of Mechanism) or to declare the gap and its owner in design.md — not to leave it unstated. That spec's `All five sections present` scenario also goes stale.

findings.title: The boundary residency sweep's slot enumeration does not include the Mechanism section
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: ENUMERATE] orbit/specs/orbit-explore-modifications/spec.md:161 closes the residency domain explicitly: material must be file-resident in Decisions, an open question's Standing recommendation slot, Considered & out, or References. A closure form or domain member worked out in conversation has no listed home, so the sweep — the mechanism that keeps the file honest before every emit — is blind to exactly the content this change adds. Add Mechanism to that enumeration in a MODIFIED delta (same capability) and mirror it in explore.ts:477.

findings.title: The three closure forms are themselves an enumeration that declares no closure form
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: ENUMERATE] `closure has exactly three DECLARED forms` is a rule with a domain (the ways closure can be justified) and the requirement two lines later says an enumeration naming no form is unclosed. The delta, design D3 and Case 9(a) all assert three without declaring which form justifies the three. Case 9(a)'s derivation — `a justification exists or it does not` — would be DERIVED over a structure the author invented, which design.md itself names as the loophole DERIVED leaves open. Declare it (BOUNDED with a stated residual is the honest option) or state that the taxonomy is exempt and why; reasoning that the three are closed because the closure rule says so is circular.

findings.title: `A Decision states exactly one of three things` is falsified by the change's own record — entries state a fact AND embed a rule
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: ENUMERATE] D-rc13-2 is classified `finding | n/a` by Case 8, yet its CONSEQUENCE clause is a rule over a set of situations: `the question to ask of ANY replacement is not will people game it but does it track the thing at all`. D-rc13-10 is classified `position | n/a` and closes with `If the proposal review shows it is over, the corollary says SPLIT — not shrink`, a conditional governing every over-ceiling stage. The situation test classifies both as RULES; the artifact's own audit classifies them as not-rules. Fix the partition: a Decision ENTRY may carry more than one claim, so the test applies per CLAIM, not per entry — and say what an entry whose rule-clause is incidental owes.

findings.title: The six-move scenario mandates an executed case per rule — a heavier bar than the cure the change rejected, and one no exemplar meets
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: COHERE] The scenario requires each rule's entry to record all six moves including `at least one executed case with a concrete input and the output it produced`, while D1 and proposal.md argue the unit is NOT an executed case and the emit rung checks closure ONLY. The change's own Mechanism section is organized per CASE, not per RULE, and contains no entry meeting this scenario for D-rc13-13 or D-rc13-14 — so the shipped convention has no worked instance anywhere. Either soften the scenario (record the six moves' dispositions per rule, EXECUTE satisfiable as `not executed — reason`) or produce one conforming exemplar and task it.

findings.title: Task 4.4 cites `the #12 lesson`, which is not what issue #12 is about
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: READ] `#12` appears nowhere in orbit/, CLAUDE.md or the architecture docs; issue #12 on the fork is `Delta scope: a MODIFIED delta cannot change non-requirement baseline prose`, unrelated to payload references. The lesson the task describes is the archive-table gap recorded in CLAUDE.md and carried by rc01's charter. Cite that, or name the real referent — an unresolvable citation in a task is a READ failure of the kind this change ships a move to prevent.

findings.title: D-rc13-5/D-rc13-6's non-negotiable prerequisite is gone (rc03a WITHDRAWN) and no promoted artifact records it
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: READ] D-rc13-5 states `Timing is not negotiable: it lands BEFORE rc13's own system review runs a blind pair, or rc13's control measurement is taken on an anchored pair`, and D-rc13-6 says the rc03a declaration `has not been performed`. Both are now false: the arc doc declares the stage then withdraws it, the conflict is folded into rc03 and remains LIVE. The file's own convention is to annotate overtaken decisions in place (D-rc13-8/9 carry marks); these two carry none, and proposal/design/tasks are silent on what rc13's own blind pair now runs against. Annotate both and record in design.md's Risks what the withdrawal costs rc13's measurement.

findings.title: No task sweeps the `five-section` residue the format change invalidates
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: ENUMERATE] Live occurrences that become wrong on ship: emit-composition.ts:908 (the missing-section warning a user sees), explore-counter.ts:12, explore.ts:365/:393/:418, onboard.ts:79, propose.ts:154-156. Section 1 and 6.1 imply the explore.ts edits but no task names the sweep, and change-completeness is what catches the rest. Add an explicit residue task listing the files.

findings.title: The requirement title still says `five-section format` while defining six sections
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: COHERE] Keeping the header verbatim is correct for MODIFIED matching and the base_fingerprints key, but three other baselines cite it by that name (orbit-explore-modifications:119, orbit-audit-drift:148, orbit-emit-composition:331) and the title will read as false in baseline forever. Either state the deferral in the delta prose (`the name is retained for delta identity; the format is six sections`) or do a deliberate REMOVED+ADDED rename with citations updated — noting that per issue #12 a MODIFIED delta cannot change the title anyway.

findings.title: The named gap flows verbatim into the orientation `next` line with no bound on length or shape
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: EXECUTE] orientation.ts:410,428 copies the trail's `next_recommended` into the workstream `next` unchanged, and the requirement's own text says a downstream reader parses the leading token. An exploration with several open rules would render an unbounded, possibly multi-line `next`. Bound the rendering: single line, a stated cap (first three ids plus `+N more`), and say what identifies a rule in the text (the decision id, not its prose).

findings.title: Exit criterion 2 asks the recommendation to name what is missing PER RULE; the delta names only which rules are open
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: CONFORM] Charter exit (2): `the emit's recommendation names what is missing per rule rather than a decision count`. The delta names the rules whose domains are open — defensible, but `what is missing` and `which rule` are different claims, and the gap is where an exit criterion gets judged generously later. Either state in design.md that naming the rule IS naming what is missing, or extend the rendering to say which part is absent (no enumeration / no declared form).

findings.title: The arc doc's rc13 charter and status log still carry the superseded grammar-keyed rule test
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: COHERE] `a Decision that states a CONDITIONAL has a domain` survives in the rc13 charter and again in the status log, while D-rc13-14 supersedes it precisely because it keys on grammar. Tasks 7.2/7.3 already carve out architect-tier work; add one entry correcting the charter's trigger sentence so the program doc does not teach the retired test after this ships.

findings.title: The promoted sketch is stale on its face
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: READ] `NOT YET DECLARED: writing a stage into orbit/architecture/clean-up-review-cycle.md is an ARCHITECT act` — the stage WAS declared and then withdrawn on 2026-09-15. The sketch travelled into the change directory and will archive as a factual claim that is false. Add a one-line dated header recording the withdrawal, or drop the file.

findings.title: The Mechanism section ships as prose rules, not as template slots — against the precedent quoted in the requirement being modified
findings.recommendation: [MOVE: NONE] The baseline text this delta carries forward states the D5 lesson verbatim: `AIs fill template slots far more reliably than they obey prose rules`, which is why `Standing recommendation:` is a slot. The six moves and the closure declaration arrive as prose obligations with no scaffolded shape; task 5.3 asserts only that the prose appears in the generated body. Consider a per-rule entry skeleton in the explore.md template (rule id, domain, closure form, the six move lines) so the affordance matches its own cited evidence. CLASSIFIED **NONE**: this is an authoring-medium choice, not a way the mechanism is wrong — no move in the set ranges over `is this the right medium for the rule`, which is itself a datum for the set's closure.

stale_suppressed.evidence: Diffed BOTH modified blocks against baseline line-for-line: orbit-conventions:118-136 — all three baseline scenarios present, prose preserved verbatim including the D5 parenthetical; orbit-run-summary-emit:192-217 — all four baseline scenarios present plus one new, and the trailing canonical-token paragraph preserved. commentary: MOVE CLASSIFICATION (the live test of this change's own scheme, run on findings it was not derived from): ENUMERATE 9, COHERE 5, READ 3, EXECUTE 2, CONFORM 2, NONE 1, FALSIFY 0. The strongest part of this change is the part it was forced into: the derivation-over-list argument and the DERIVED/SOURCED/BOUNDED declaration are load-bearing, and the explore record earns them rather than asserting them — Case 7 destroying a set ratified an hour earlier is the most persuasive evidence in the file. What worries me is that the change applies its instrument to rc03a's record and then stops. The six moves were never classified against rc02's four CRITICALs, which sit in the same explore.md as Case 1, and one of them (`assignCadence` blowup) does not land anywhere in the set; R-crc-7's own rationale names a usability class the set also misses. By the change's own corollary — classification falsifies, never closes — running the one extra classification it already had the data for was the cheapest possible test of its central claim, and skipping it is the same move Case 8 describes: a rule not mechanically scheduled does not get applied to the artifact that invented it. The second pattern is that the change edits one of two copies of nearly everything. The explore.md format is defined in orbit-conventions AND in orbit-explore-modifications; the mode-resolution rule lives in `Three invocation modes supported` AND in the new re-entry requirement; the section list is restated again in orbit-propose-modifications and in three body templates. Modifying one copy and adding beside the other produces exactly the COHERE defect the change names as most-recurring — and in the propose case quietly leaves the Mechanism section with no route out of explore, so the stage's deliverable stops at the promotion boundary. Third, the emit half is the half that makes the convention non-advisory, and it is currently the half with no mechanism behind it: everything downstream of `maturityRecommendation` is well-specified prose about what the rung should say, and nothing says what it reads, who computes it, or how a deliberately grammar-independent, engine-unjudgeable property becomes a function argument. Related, the domain `every rule in Decisions` was never enumerated against a real Decisions section — the change's own, which contains superseded rules and rules explicitly handed to other stages, would be permanently withheld from the top rung by the requirement as written. That is the finding I would most want resolved before implementation, because it is the change failing its own ENUMERATE move on its own file.
